summary: Ti-doped ZnO (TZO) films with thicknesses ranging from 24 to 284 nm were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films showed a change in preferred orientation from c-axis to a-axis with increasing thickness. The electrical and optical properties were found to be thickness-dependent, with the lowest resistivity achieved for the thickest film. The study also suggested that the films grow in a hexagonal bipyramidal form.
evidence: Highly conductive and transparent titanium-doped zinc oxide (TZO) films with thicknesses ranging from 24 to 284 nm were deposited using atomic layer deposition. The TZO films change preferred orientation from c-axis orientation to a-axis orientation with increasing film thickness. The lowest resistivity of 2.0x10-3 cm was achieved for the largest film thickness. The transmittance and reflectance of the TZO films show thickness-dependent properties in the IR region caused by changes in carrier concentration, increasing carrier absorption and changing the plasma frequency to higher energy wavelengths. The investigation of ALD growth rates and composition of the TZO films using the current set of precursors are described elsewhere. The preferred orientation in ZnO depositions by ALD has previously been shown to vary with temperature, dopant concentration, pulse and purge lengths, electric field and substrate. The grain size on the surface in the horizontal plane increase significantly with increasing thickness. The electrical properties of TZO films are clearly thickness-dependent up to 200 nm. The electrical properties improve significantly with increasing thickness as both carrier concentration and mobility increases. Thickness-dependent optical properties are found in the IR regime as carrier absorption and the plasma frequency change with thickness, caused by increasing carrier concentration for larger film thicknesses. The study also suggested that the films grow in a hexagonal bipyramidal form, not as a prismatic shape.
